description:
Semantic (dense-vector) search over the tenant's chunks.

Use for conceptual questions ("how does X work", "anything about Y").
Returns passages semantically related to the query with a relevance
score (higher = better). For exact-term lookups use ``search_keyword``;
when you want both at once use ``search_hybrid``.

Each hit carries a ``chunk_id``, ``materialized_path`` and a ``text``
snippet. Recommended follow-ups:

* ``cite(chunk_id)`` — get a structured citation for the answer.
* ``read_around(chunk_id, radius=2)`` — pull surrounding context.
* ``read(path_part_id=chunk_id)`` — fetch the full chunk body.

chunk_types.description: Only return chunks of these types (e.g. [TABLE] to find tabular data).
chunk_types.title: Chunk Types

parent_path_part_ids.description: Restrict search to descendants of these path-parts. Omit for whole tenant.
parent_path_part_ids.title: Parent Path Part Ids

tag_ids.description: Only include chunks whose document carries all these tag UUIDs.
tag_ids.title: Tag Ids

top_k.description: Max number of chunks to return (1-50).
top_k.title: Top K

name: search_knowledge

chunk_id.description: Stable id for this chunk. Use it with `cite`, `read_around`, `view_chunk_image`, or `read` (which now also accepts a chunk_id). NOT the same as `path_part_id`.
chunk_id.title: Chunk Id

materialized_path.description: Full root-to-leaf path of the chunk (e.g. `Folder/SubFolder/Document/Section/...`). Use this when displaying citations or grouping hits by document.
materialized_path.title: Materialized Path

path_part_id.description: PDO id of the chunk node in the path tree. Pass to `get_info` for ancestry; do NOT confuse with `chunk_id` — they are different UUIDs.
path_part_id.title: Path Part Id

score.description: Relevance score from the search backend (higher = better).
score.title: Score
